tier_reason: Upgraded from C to B on stronger evidence: the peer-reviewed FAST '14 paper (Rumble, Kejriwal, Ousterhout, 'Log-structured Memory for DRAM-based Storage', Section 8.7, Figure 12) measures RAMCloud against Redis 2.6.14 and HyperDex on YCSB and shows RAMCloud ahead on the read-heavy workloads. It is not A because the paper gives no compiler or flags and no YCSB driver path, and the original wiki page only contrasts with memcached in words (5us/15us, '10-1000x faster than other available alternatives'), which alone would be C.

corrections.workload: YCSB workloads A, B, C, D, F (E omitted, no scans), 1 KB objects, 100M operations per client, 24 YCSB clients on 24 nodes against 12 storage-server nodes, triple replication; Redis 2.6.14 and HyperDex 1.0rc4 used kernel sockets over Infiniband, and RAMCloud ran both with kernel sockets and with its kernel-bypass Infiniband Verbs transport at 75% and 90% memory utilisation
corrections.claimed_speedup: FAST '14 paper, Figure 12: RAMCloud outperforms Redis on the read-heavy YCSB workloads B, C and D with both kernel sockets and Verbs, and the Verbs transport 'more than doubles read throughput' compared with RAMCloud on kernel sockets. On the write-heavy workloads A and F, RAMCloud with kernel sockets trails Redis, and with Verbs it matches Redis write throughput at 75% utilisation but is 25% slower than Redis on workload A at 90%. Exact per-bar values appear only in the figure. Separately, the project wiki claims reads in as little as 5us and writes under 15us, calling RAMCloud '10-1000x faster than other available alternatives', and contrasts it with memcached only in words.
corrections.hardware: 80-node cluster: Xeon X3470 (4x2.93 GHz, 3.6 GHz Turbo), 24 GB DDR3-800, 2x Crucial M4 128 GB SSDs, Mellanox ConnectX-2 Infiniband HCA, Mellanox SX6036 4X FDR switch, Linux 2.6.32
corrections.caveats: The win over Redis holds only for the read-heavy workloads; RAMCloud trails or ties Redis on write-heavy YCSB A/F. The comparison is not like-for-like on durability: RAMCloud waits for synchronous triple replication, while Redis used append-only logging with a 1s fsync and asynchronous replicas. The best RAMCloud numbers need Infiniband kernel bypass (Verbs). The baseline is Redis 2.6.14 from 2013, and the paper is by the RAMCloud authors. Exact values are only in a bar chart, and no compiler or flags are stated. The wiki's 5us/15us and '10-1000x' figures are marketing with no methodology, and the memcached contrast is qualitative only (the TOCS 2015 paper cites ~300us memcached latency at Facebook from a personal communication, not from a benchmark). The project is marked 'No Longer Maintained', with its last commit in 2019. GitHub reports the license as NOASSERTION, but the LICENSE file is plain ISC.

notes: The wiki page does contain the quoted 5us/15us and '10-1000x' text, but it names memcached only in words, so I switched the record's evidence to the FAST '14 YCSB comparison against Redis, which is peer-reviewed. The record's metric should become 'throughput' because the paper compares throughput and metric is not a correctable field. If the orchestrator wants memcached kept as the baseline, the tier falls back to C. Metadata checked: ISC LICENSE file, not a fork, not archived, 503 stars, last commit 2019-10-16, abandoned.

tier_reason: The README Benchmarks section shows first-party memtier_benchmark tables against Redis on an AMD Ryzen 7 4800H, and every quoted number matches (130,019 vs 135,165; 1,119,012 vs 1,823,366; 1,718,018 vs 5,178,742 = 3.01x; 4.23x at pipeline=500). It stays C, not A: the memtier command lines are not scripted in the repo, the compiler and Redis version used are not stated, and benchmarks/ holds only Google Benchmark microbenchmarks.

corrections.workload: memtier_benchmark (8 threads, 25 clients/thread, CPU-pinned via taskset) against RapidKV and Redis on the same machine, with Redis persistence disabled and both servers restarted between runs. Runs: baseline pipeline=1, 1:1 SET:GET, 8B values, 100K keys; mixed pipeline=16, 1:9 SET:GET, 64B values, 200K keys; pipeline-depth sweep (1/10/100/200/500), 1:9 SET:GET, 8B values, 1M keys, 30s runs; plus 2KB-value (pipeline=64), SET-only 128B and GET-only runs
corrections.compiler_and_flags: Compiler used for the benchmarks not stated (README requires GCC 12+/Clang 15+/MSVC 2022+); the CMakeLists Release build uses -O3 -march=native -flto on GCC/Clang
corrections.caveats: The benchmark is first-party and self-run with no independent verification. The compiler and Redis version are not stated, Redis io-threads settings are not stated, and the memtier command lines are not scripted in the repo (Tier C). The 4.2x headline is the best case at pipeline=500; at pipeline=1, throughput is at parity (+4% in one run, 0.99x in the sweep). The comparison is not feature-equivalent: RapidKV is single-threaded with string-only values, no persistence, replication, AUTH or TLS, and 13 commands against Redis's 400+. The repo has 1 star, and its first commit was 2026-01-31.

notes: The README also has Google Benchmark microbenchmarks against std: its FlatMap is 1.5-2.6x faster than std::unordered_map, and CompactString is up to 5.8x faster than std::string on moves. These could matter for the C++-first catalog, but compiler and flags for those runs are not stated either. Metadata checked: MIT, not a fork, not archived, 1 star, last commit 2026-05-10 (active).
